collections.title: Your sketch kitchen
collections.description: One choice above the small prep sink; appliance tower and primary-sink drying storage stay fixed.
assumptions: The OTG, microwave and PRIMARY washing-sink drying cabinet are fixed in both variants. Only the shallow upper above the SMALL food-prep sink is optional.

Both variants share the updated 380 mm right-end crockery showcase, with two tinted-glass faces, warm lighting and decorative crockery. The adjacent prep slab is 1350 mm; total room dimensions remain 3400 x 4580 mm.
The original 3400 x 4580 mm layout, sinks, worktops, two-face-open decorative display and 300 mm-deep shutter garage are retained.
Generic procedural appliances are placeholders, not selected products. OTG body 480 W x 420 D x 340 H mm; microwave body 480 W x 390 D x 300 H mm. Handles and feet are additional.

The open appliance niches illustrate placement only. A normal countertop OTG is NOT assumed safe to operate in cabinetry. Manufacturer approval, heat resistance, clearances, ventilation, door opening, access and electrical requirements must be checked before specifying any product or enclosure.
Illustrative empty gaps around appliances are not certified thermal clearances. No sliding support or modeled gap is a safety guarantee.

The primary-sink drying cabinet contains a real modeled wire dish rack, plates and a removable drip tray behind closed matching fronts. Tray emptying/access and cabinet moisture protection need detailing; no drainage connection is modeled or verified.
Prep-sink upper is 600 mm frontage x 320 mm deep, elevations 1600 to 2350 mm, with an under-cabinet task strip. Clear mode has no upper cabinet and uses a slim wall-mounted task light.
Interactive GLB uses approximate PBR, not the Cycles poster appearance. Procedural textures and lighting are simplified; no external assets or URLs are required.

collections.title: Fresh start - whole-floor concept
collections.description: A new three-bedroom, three-bathroom arrangement: open kitchen/dining, central family living, a mandir/reading corner and a relocated shared shower room. Prior layouts are unchanged.
assumptions: Entirely new interior concept, not a surveyed, structurally assessed or approved construction plan.
Three bedrooms and three bathrooms retained by assumption while the owner was unavailable.
Existing outer footprint, external openings, stair-access location and open-to-sky void retained. No floor or roof is invented over the OTS or stair region.

One new 1.10 m living-room window is proposed on the east facade for direct daylight; structure, permissions and external conditions are unverified. The existing window now serving the common bathroom is frosted for privacy.
Original internal walls are replaced by the proposed partitions. Load-bearing walls, columns, beams and services are unknown: demolition is NOT authorized by this visualization.
North/south mean plan-up/down, not surveyed compass directions.
The guest bedroom uses the former drawing-room zone; former bedroom 2 becomes shared living plus a relocated common shower room.
Bathroom relocation, drainage gradients, waste-stack connections, ventilation and waterproofing need specialist site design.
Ceiling height 3.0 m, opening elevations, furnishings and appliance envelopes are provisional. Manufacturer thermal, electrical and maintenance requirements take precedence.
The mandir's location and empty altar are proposals; deity imagery, religious orientation and ritual requirements are not assumed. Electric lighting only.
External doors are preserved, but no unprovided balcony, landing or other exterior accommodation is invented.
This concept preserves no presumed approved interior layout; earlier Blender and CAD versions remain separate and unchanged.

collections.description: A 900 mm partition shift creates a separate sink-and-dishwasher service bay, reached through a sliding glass door. Fridge, microwave and OTG remain inside the kitchen. The original OTS void is retained.
assumptions: Layout proposal, not approved construction. Wall alterations, lintels, services, daylight, extraction and local requirements need site/professional review.
Appliance envelopes are generic design allowances, not manufacturer installation specifications. Confirm selected models, opening sweeps, heat gaps and servicing space.

collections.title: Earlier - Option A - Oak and limestone
collections.description: Light oak cabinetry, a pale stone worktop and the existing peninsula. The former kitchen window is replaced by a three-door wall-cabinet run. A timber-framed mandir with a quiet stone backdrop sits beside the lounge sofa.
assumptions: All changes are visualization proposals, not approved construction instructions.
The kitchen-to-OTS window is removed and its opening infilled in this proposal, making space for an approximately 1.67 m wide, 0.35 m deep three-door wall-cabinet run above the counter.

Closing the window removes a source of natural light and ventilation. The remaining glazed utility entrance is not assumed to satisfy ventilation requirements; daylight, extraction, wall infill, cabinet fixing and local requirements need professional/site review.
With user approval, the utility door and narrow adjacent window become one approximately 1.70 m two-panel glazed opening. One panel slides over the fixed panel.
The slider's approximately 0.77 m fully-open clear width, lintel, wall alterations, safety glazing, ventilation and waterproofing require professional/site review.
The mandir reuses the lounge-side cabinet footprint marked in the screenshot. Its altar and storage are provisional; no deity, religious orientation or ritual requirements have been assumed.
Mandir lighting is electric. No flame, incense or heat-source placement is specified beside the timber joinery and upholstered sofa.
The bed change is a reversible interpretation pending review: Bedroom 1's headboard is centred on the plan-top wall, left of the wardrobe. The existing bed and bedside sizes are retained.
The WC and shower are swapped within Bedroom 1's en-suite. Soil/waste connections, falls, waterproofing and service access require a plumber/site review; no service routing is designed.
Existing room geometry and furniture outside the kitchen, mandir, Bedroom 1 bed group and its en-suite WC/shower remain from the v001 baseline.
